title: REFLECT: Summarizing Robot Experiences for Failure Explanation and Correction
models: GPT-4 (and GPT-3.5 comparison) as failure reasoner and planner; MDETR, CLIP, AudioCLIP for perception; no VLA policy (scripted primitives in AI2THOR, teleoperated UR5e)
methods: hierarchical multisensory summary: scene graphs from RGB-D, object states, audio events, subgoal verification
progressive LLM querying: check subgoals, then explain execution or planning failure and localize its time
LLM correction planner conditioned on the explanation
question: Can an LLM, given a structured summary of a robot's multisensory experience, explain and localize failures and use the explanation to plan a correction?
key_findings: Simulation (Table 1): REFLECT explanation accuracy 88.4% / 84.2%, localization 96.0% / 80.7%, correction-plan success 79.1% / 80.7% for execution / planning failures.
Correction planning without the explanation is much worse (41.9% / 56.1%), so the explanation is useful for recovery.
Removing audio lowers execution-failure explanation and localization by about 20%.
Real-world performance drops somewhat due to perception errors.
RoboFail taxonomy: 55% planning failures (wrong actions, missing actions, wrong order, ambiguous reference) and 45% execution failures.

benchmarks: RoboFail: 100 simulated failure scenarios (10 tasks x 10) and 30 real-world failure scenarios (11 tasks)
evidence.scale: 100 sim + 30 real failure cases; explanations judged by human evaluators
evidence.baselines: BLIP2 captions, w/o sound, w/o progressive querying, subgoal-only summary, LLM text summary, correction without explanation

causal_validation: None on any model internals; the explanation is an external LLM account of behavior. Correction success after using the explanation is a behavioral test of usefulness.
closed_loop: Correction plans are executed to measure task success; explanations are generated post hoc from recorded experience.
limitations_stated: Assumes ground-truth detection in simulation; real-world perception errors reduce performance.
Failures in the real dataset come from a human teleoperator mimicking policies, not from a learned policy.
critique: An external, post-hoc explainer of robot behavior: it explains what went wrong in the world, not why a policy chose its actions, so it is complementary to (not a substitute for) internals-based interpretability.
Injected or teleoperated failures and scripted primitives are much easier to explain than failures of end-to-end VLAs, whose errors are often subtle motion-level problems (see SAFE, FailureSpot).
Representative of the slow VLM-supervisor approach that later VLA failure detectors (SAFE, Hide-and-Seek) contrast against for latency.
one_line: REFLECT turns multisensory robot logs into a hierarchical text summary that GPT-4 uses to explain and localize failures and to plan corrections, reaching about 80% correction success on injected failures in simulation.
